sections.title: Not another dashboard
body: Most developer tools answer “what could we measure?” with a wall of charts. Someone then has to read them, decide what matters, and remember to come back.
Your day doesn’t need more charts. It needs the one decision worth making.
sections.caption: A wall of charts, and the one card that needs you.

sections.title: One thing, with its receipt
body: Sensei opens on Today: a single finding that needs a decision, with its provenance, the sessions it came from, one click away. Below it sit at most three supporting insights, your first-turn resolution trend, and your most recent sessions.
The receipt matters. You can check the evidence before you act, rather than trusting a score.

sections.title: Observe, find, act
body: Every part of Sensei works the same way. It observes the work, forms one finding, and offers one action: Apply, Review or Dismiss.
The action feeds the next round of observation, so a dismissed finding teaches as much as an applied one.

sections.title: At first, it just listens
body: A mentor who gives advice on day one is guessing. Until enough of your work has been watched, Today says “Still listening…” and offers no action at all.
Once there is enough signal across your projects, it switches over and findings start. That threshold is decided by the daemon from what it has actually seen, not by a timer.

sections.title: Now, soon, settled
body: Insights are sorted for you into three columns: Now (needs a decision), Soon (still building evidence) and Settled (decided or adopted).
Each asks for a single decision with a sensible default, and one decision moves it along.

sections.title: See what it adopted for you
body: Some of what Sensei learns it adopts on your behalf: memories your assistant loads at the start of the next relevant session. Each one is laid open: what it is, why it exists, how it applies, where, and a seven-day strip of how often it was used.
You can reinforce or challenge any of them, and a memory with enough support can be promoted to a rule.

takeaway: One thing today, with its receipt.
takeawaySub: Sensei turns watching into one decision.
